column1: # *** THE JOHANNESBURG CEMETERY REGISTER ANSWERS THE 1999 QUESTION. 20 September 2026. ***

column2: 6X6S-M484, M48C, M48H, M48Z - Pierre, Richard, Gayle, Jeffrey.
column4: *** Four sequential entries in one register. *** The family was entered together, in one act of registration, on 18 November 1999. *** That is structural corroboration on top of the dates ***, and it is the kind of thing an index loses and a register keeps.

*** ROW 20 IS ANSWERED AND ROW 17 IS SMALLER FOR IT. *** She was the last person in this family whose dates rested on the commercial index - 'born 1921, died 1999' stood only as *** their *** fact. *** It is now free-sourced, with a day. *** She was Ricardo Juan Carlos's widow, aged 78, and she died *** five days after *** the other four and was buried two days *** before *** them.
*** ROW 106 wanted a date for the third person in the Newlands grave *** and had only 'born and died 1947'. *** Here is the day. ***

column2: *** Rhena May Lerena *** b.1913, d. *** 1 April 1998 ***, buried *** 9 April 1998 ***, Braamfontein. *** Ricardo Juan Carlos *** b.1920, d. 21 December 1994, buried 28 December 1994.
column4: Both already held, both now matched exactly by a second source. *** Rhena is the control this archive used on 17 September to prove the gazette misses real adult deaths - and she is HERE ***, which shows the cemetery register catches what the gazette drops.

column1: *** A TRAP IN THIS COLLECTION, AND IT WOULD HAVE COST A CENTURY ***
column2: The index renders *** Doreen's year as '0099' and Ricardo's as '0094' *** - the '19' is dropped.
column4: *** Read literally, Doreen May Lerena died in the year 99 and Ricardo in 94. *** Any script sorting or filtering this collection by year will put them in the first century. *** The full dates are recoverable only because the day and month survive and the burial sequence fixes them. ***
